message.reasoning:
I need to make a Monopoly decision.

I am analyzing my current position. I own Mediterranean Avenue, Electric Company, and Boardwalk. My cash is $938.

I am reviewing the other players. p1 has a dangerous orange monopoly with three houses on each property. p2 has cash of $1256 and no monopolies. p4 has cash of $513 and holds several properties including Penn RR, Ventnor, and Park Place.

I rejected p4's offer for Park Place. A $700 trade would leave only $238, which is too risky against the $600 rent on New York with three houses.

I am now weighing post-turn options: end_turn, propose_trade, or mortgage_property.

Rebuilding the brown set by trading Baltic Avenue back from p2 seems unwise. The rent and building costs are too low to reliably threaten other players.

I am recalculating the exact orange monopoly rent values. I need to confirm whether three houses on New York, Tennessee, or St. James Place can reliably bankrupt p1 with only $98 cash.

The exact orange monopoly rent values are now confirmed. Three houses on New York Avenue, Tennessee Avenue, and St. James Place charge $750, $700, and $550 respectively. These are lethal against a player with only $98 cash.

I am now calculating the mortgage value of my own properties to see if I can raise enough money to survive these upcoming rent payments.

Mortgaging all properties would raise $305, giving a total survival capacity of $1243. I can survive one orange rent hit cleanly from cash alone, but a second hit could bankrupt me. I am now weighing whether to trade or simply end my turn.

I am now calculating the exact brown monopoly rent values. Even a hotel on Baltic Avenue would charge $450, which could bankrupt p1. However, the probability of p1 landing on brown before I land on orange is low. Building houses on brown would also drain cash needed to survive the orange monopoly. This trade is not urgent.

Baltic Avenue is too expensive to reclaim from p2. The light blue and yellow monopolies are unattainable without hurting myself. I am now checking whether the green properties are unowned.

Pennsylvania Avenue is green, not yellow. p4 owns it and Ventnor, which is yellow. No green monopoly exists yet.

Red properties are split between p2 and unowned spaces. The dark blue deadlock with p4 is settled; re-proposing the same deal would look weak. I am now considering a trade with p1.

I decided against trading with p1. They hold the orange monopoly and cannot build a fourth house with only $98 cash, so giving them money would be counterproductive. I am now looking for a cheap trade that could create a new monopoly for me.

I am now evaluating a trade with p2 for Baltic Avenue. They have no use for it since they already own Reading, Indiana, and Marvin Gardens. I would need to pay a premium because they know I want the property to complete my brown set. The cost of building three houses on both brown properties is $300, which makes this trade unattractive.

I am now calculating the exact bankruptcy risk from a developed Baltic Avenue. Three houses would charge $180, which exceeds p1's $98 cash and could bankrupt them. If they land there and cannot pay, I would inherit their orange monopoly. However, p1 is currently on Tennessee, so the probability of landing on brown before I land on orange is low.

I am mapping the board positions to check if I will land on orange properties before p1 can reach brown.

I am on Baltic Avenue (position 3). The next rolls will take me toward light blue and pinks, then around to the orange properties near positions 16 through 19. That is 13 to 16 spaces away.

I will end my turn. Rebuilding brown would waste cash and reduce my survival buffer before the orange danger hits. I have no debt, so mortgaging is unnecessary.
